name: The dark lamp under the microscope
subject: practical_science
brief: In the biology practical at Nabapara Vidyalaya, three students are sharing one compound microscope to sketch onion-root mitosis stages. When the substage rocker switch is pressed, the 6-volt halogen lamp beneath the condenser stays dark. Because the other two students are waiting to draw, you cannot keep the instrument dismantled for long.

causes.name: The brass 15-ampere bench wall socket has tripped its breaker
The spring cap on the microscope's base glass-fuse holder has worked loose half a turn
The rotary brightness rheostat in the base has an open carbon track
The 6-volt, 20-watt bi-pin halogen capsule filament has burned through

tests.name: Look at the red neon indicator on the bench wall socket and feel the base fuse cap
Unscrew the knurled fuse cap on the heel of the stand and inspect the dimmer knob stop
Measure AC voltage at the bench socket and after the dimmer wiper
Measure continuity across the base fuse holder terminals before and after tightening the cap
Fit the demonstrator's spare 6-volt halogen capsule into the ceramic lampholder

note: Set in the biology room at Nabapara Vidyalaya (loc_nhss). The spring cap of the fuse holder in the microscope's base has backed out half a turn, so the lamp circuit is open though the wall socket is live. Looking at the wall neon and then the fuse cap isolates it.
